topics.title: Approaches to classification and Koeppen's scheme
topics.ncert_sections: Koeppen's Scheme of Classification of Climate

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between empirical, genetic and applied approaches to classifying climate.
Explain how Koeppen used temperature, precipitation and letter codes to define climatic groups and types.
Describe the location and features of the Af, Am and Aw climate types.
Explain where and why dry climates occur at low and middle latitudes.
Compare subtropical steppe and desert climates.
Explain the location and the hot dry summer and rainy winter of the Mediterranean climate.
Describe the Cwa, Cfa and Cfb climate types and their locations.

topics.title: Cold snow forest and polar climates (Groups D and E)
topics.ncert_sections: Cold Snow Forest Climates (D); Polar Climates (E)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the distribution and features of the Df and Dw climate types.
Describe the tundra climate, permafrost and its vegetation.
Explain the features of the ice cap climate and how icebergs form.

topics.title: Climate change: evidence and the past
topics.ncert_sections: Climate Change; Climate in the recent past

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the geological, biological and historical evidence that climate changes naturally.
Recall major climatic episodes of the geological and recent past, including India.
Explain sunspots and Milankovitch oscillations as astronomical causes of climate change.
Explain how volcanic aerosols and human greenhouse gas emissions change climate.
Explain the greenhouse effect using the analogy of a glasshouse.
Identify the main greenhouse gases, their sources and sinks, and what makes a GHG effective.
Interpret the 20th-century temperature record, the impacts of warming and the Kyoto Protocol.
